target: Ammunition depot of an arms company
title: Explosion and fire at an ammunition depot
summary: Ammunition detonated in a fire at a warehouse belonging to an arms company that supplies Ukraine.
note: The owner blames Russia but has no direct evidence. Bulgarian prosecutors have linked earlier blasts at the same company to Russian military intelligence.

target: Airports and offshore oil and gas sites
title: Drones over airports and oil and gas sites
summary: Drones were seen near offshore platforms and airports; several Russian nationals were arrested for flying drones.
note: The prime minister said it was unacceptable for foreign intelligence to fly drones over Norwegian airports.

title: Arson at a restaurant
summary: A restaurant in Gdynia was set on fire.
note: Prosecutors say it was commissioned by foreign intelligence; Poland blames Russia and Belarus for such attacks. Six people were indicted in 2025.

title: Second explosion at the same depot
summary: Explosions and a fire hit the same company's ammunition warehouses again.
note: The company suspects sabotage; the pattern matches earlier blasts that prosecutors linked to Russian military intelligence.

target: Cars of the interior minister and a journalist
title: Minister's and journalist's cars smashed
summary: The windows of the interior minister's car and a journalist's car were systematically smashed on the same night.
note: Estonia's security service said the operation was coordinated by Russian special services; a court convicted the organiser.

title: Hackers tamper with a village wastewater plant
summary: A hacker group posted footage of itself manipulating a village wastewater plant's controls.
note: Claimed by a group that US authorities say was directed by Russian military intelligence.

history.reason: Claim by an officially linked group

title: Plan to set fire to two London businesses
summary: The Leyton group planned further arson attacks on two businesses owned by a critic of the Kremlin.
note: Set out in court as part of the Wagner-directed case.

title: Hackers burst water pipes
summary: Hackers changed water pressure at a waterworks south of Copenhagen, bursting pipes.
impact: About 50 homes without water for seven hours; 450 for one hour
note: Danish defence intelligence named a group tied to the Russian state; Denmark summoned Russia's ambassador.

title: Plot to set fire to a paint factory
summary: A man was arrested while preparing to set fire to a paint factory and other targets in Wrocław.
note: A court jailed him for eight years for planning sabotage on behalf of Russia.

target: Museum of the Occupation of Latvia
title: Firebomb thrown into the Occupation Museum
summary: A window was smashed and an incendiary bottle thrown into the director's office.
note: Latvia's security service pursued the organisers on suspicion of assisting Russia.

title: Hackers open a hydro mill's valves
summary: Hackers who believed they were attacking a dam manipulated a small hydro mill's controls.
impact: Water level upstream dropped about 20 cm
note: Same group as the Wydminy attack.

history.reason: Claim by an officially linked group

title: Arson attempt at a warehouse
summary: An attempt was made to set fire to a warehouse in Gdańsk.
note: Part of the same indictment as the Gdynia restaurant fire.

target: Warehouse of the same Ukrainian firm as Leyton
title: Arson at a Ukrainian firm's warehouse
summary: A warehouse belonging to the same Ukrainian company hit in Leyton was set on fire near Madrid.
note: UK counter-terrorism police linked it to the Leyton case; no Spanish attribution found.

title: Warehouse holding aid for Ukraine set alight
summary: Two industrial units storing generators and satellite equipment bound for Ukraine were set on fire. Around 60 firefighters tackled the blaze.
impact: Around £1 million of damage; no injuries reported
note: A London jury convicted the attackers in July 2025. Prosecutors said the attack was organised through the Wagner Group on behalf of the Russian state.

title: Arson at a DIY store
summary: A large DIY store in Warsaw was set on fire.
note: Prosecutors charged a suspect as part of a group carrying out arson attacks linked to Russia. The trial is pending.

title: Arson at a pallet storage site
summary: A pallet storage facility near Warsaw was set on fire.
note: Part of the same indictment as the Gdynia restaurant fire.

title: Arson at an IKEA store
summary: An IKEA store in Vilnius was set on fire after closing hours.
note: Lithuanian prosecutors said in March 2025 that Russian military intelligence orchestrated it. Russia denies involvement.

title: Marywilska 44 shopping centre destroyed
summary: A fire destroyed Warsaw's largest shopping centre, used by many Vietnamese-run businesses.
impact: About 1,400 shops and service points destroyed
note: Poland's prime minister said in May 2025 that Russian services ordered the arson. Poland closed a Russian consulate in response.

title: Arson at a construction warehouse
summary: A construction supply warehouse in Warsaw was set on fire.
note: A suspect was charged with terrorism for acting on behalf of Russian intelligence.

history.reason: Charges by the special services coordinator

title: Arson at a construction warehouse
summary: A construction supply warehouse in Radom was set on fire; footage appeared on Russian-linked Telegram channels within hours.
note: Same suspect and charge as the Warsaw warehouse.

history.reason: Charges by the special services coordinator

title: Arson attempt on city buses
summary: An attacker set fire to buses at a Prague public transport depot; staff put the fire out.
note: The prime minister said Russian involvement was very likely. The suspect was charged with terrorism.

title: Arson at a DIY store
summary: A DIY store in Łódź caught fire; it was first blamed on poor storage of chemicals.
note: Prosecutors tie it to the parcel network they attribute to Russian military intelligence.

title: Parcel device ignites at the DHL air hub
summary: A device hidden in a parcel caught fire at Leipzig airport before loading onto a cargo flight. It was one of four parcels sent from Vilnius.
note: Lithuanian prosecutors said the network was organised by people linked to Russian military intelligence; 15 suspects have been charged.

title: Parcel device ignites in a courier truck
summary: A parcel from the same batch as the Leipzig device caught fire in a courier truck in Poland.
note: Covered by Lithuanian prosecutors' findings on the parcel network. The exact town has not been confirmed by a source.

title: Parcel fire at a DHL warehouse
summary: A parcel device ignited at a DHL warehouse. It came from the same batch as the Leipzig device.
note: Covered by Lithuanian prosecutors' findings on the parcel network.

title: Two arson attempts on equipment for Ukraine
summary: Two attempts were made to burn radio equipment made for Ukraine's armed forces; neither caused damage.
note: Prosecutors say the group acted on instructions from Russian military intelligence; six people are on trial for terrorism.

place: Baltic Sea, off Gotland and Öland
title: Two data cables cut within a day
summary: Two undersea data cables were severed near-simultaneously; a Chinese bulk carrier was investigated.
note: Germany's defence minister said nobody believed it was accidental. Swedish investigators could not establish that it was deliberate.

target: Estlink 2 power cable and telecoms cables
title: Estlink 2 power cable and telecoms cables cut
summary: A tanker allegedly dragged its anchor along the seabed, damaging a power link and several telecoms cables. Finland seized the ship.
impact: Power link and telecoms cables damaged
note: Finland and Estonia say the ship belongs to Russia's shadow fleet. A Helsinki court dismissed charges for lack of jurisdiction in October 2025; prosecutors appealed.

title: Hackers disrupt a small hydropower plant
summary: Hackers hit the same small hydropower plant twice; the second attack disrupted turbine operations.
note: Pro-Russian hacktivists are suspected; no official attribution.

title: Arson at a village supermarket
summary: A supermarket near a military training area was set on fire as a trial run.
note: An Estonian court found it was ordered by Russian military intelligence.

title: Latvia–Gotland cable break ruled an accident
summary: A data cable was severed by a ship's anchor; Sweden first investigated it as sabotage.
note: Swedish prosecutors ruled it an accident caused by bad weather, faulty anchor equipment and poor seamanship.

title: Arson at a Ukrainian-themed restaurant
summary: A window was smashed and petrol set alight inside a restaurant chosen for its pro-Ukrainian stance.
note: An Estonian court found it was ordered by Russian military intelligence.

title: Third damage to the same data cable
summary: Damage was found on a Finland–Germany data cable for the third time in three months.
note: Swedish police opened a sabotage investigation; no culprit identified.

title: Power cut to the island's water pump
summary: Someone opened an electrical cabinet and disconnected power to a pump supplying much of the island's water.
impact: Pump stopped for a few hours; drinking water unaffected
note: Police confirmed deliberate interference; the security service is aware; no suspect named.

title: Dam controls hijacked, floodgate opened
summary: Intruders took control of a dam's remote controls and opened a floodgate for about four hours before staff noticed.
impact: About 500 litres a second released; no injuries
note: Norway's security police attributed it in August 2025 to pro-Russian cyber actors. Russia's embassy called the claim unfounded.

title: Hackers change settings at a water plant
summary: Attackers accessed a water plant's control system and changed flushing cycles.
note: Poland's security agency confirmed the breach and said such groups are often fronts for Russian intelligence, without naming a culprit.

target: Properties and a car linked to the prime minister
title: Fires at properties linked to the prime minister
summary: A car and two homes linked to the UK prime minister were set on fire over five days.
note: UK officials examined whether Russia recruited the suspects. Russia denied involvement.

title: Hackers change pump and filter settings
summary: An intruder used an administrator account to change pump, filter and alarm settings at a water plant.
note: Confirmed by Poland's security agency in the same report as Szczytno.

title: Airport closure over reported drones
summary: Copenhagen airport closed for nearly four hours after reported drone sightings; the government called it a hybrid attack at the time.
impact: Flights halted for nearly four hours
note: After a nine-month investigation, Danish police said they could not confirm there had been drone activity.

title: Airport closure over a reported drone
summary: Oslo airport closed its airspace for about three hours after a reported drone sighting.
impact: Flights diverted for about three hours
note: Norwegian police shelved the case in November 2025, unable to confirm the sightings were drones.

target: Airport, plus sites at Esbjerg, Sønderborg and Skrydstrup air base
title: Drones close Aalborg airport
summary: Drones were seen over Aalborg airport and several other Danish sites overnight; the airport closed for about three hours.
impact: Airport closed for about three hours
note: The government called it a systematic hybrid attack by a professional actor. No culprit was named; Russia denied involvement.

target: Power plant, refinery, shipyard and military sites
title: Drones over energy and defence sites
summary: Drones flew over a power plant, a refinery, a submarine shipyard and government buildings on two nights.
note: The state interior minister said a possible espionage operation was being investigated.

title: Drones over Denmark's largest air base
summary: Drones were seen inside and outside the air base perimeter; its airspace was briefly closed.
note: Part of the late-September wave the government called a hybrid attack; no link made for this incident.

title: Drone sightings halt Munich airport
summary: Drone sightings grounded flights at Munich airport on two consecutive nights.
impact: Dozens of flights disrupted; thousands of passengers affected
note: Germany's chancellor said he assumed Russia was behind most of the drone flights.

title: Fifteen drones over a military camp
summary: About 15 drones circled a military camp before flying into German airspace.
note: The defence ministry is examining links to foreign powers, including Russia.

title: Drones over army headquarters
summary: Drones flew over key parts of an army brigade headquarters on two nights.
note: The defence minister called it an orchestrated operation; Russian involvement not confirmed.

title: Drones over an air base three nights running
summary: Drones flew over the air base on consecutive nights; attempts to jam or shoot them down failed.
note: The defence minister pointed to Russia's methods and motives but said there was no formal evidence.

title: Drones halt Liège cargo airport
summary: Drone sightings suspended flights at Liège for about six hours.
impact: Flights suspended for about six hours
note: Belgian security services reportedly see Russia behind the wave; no formal attribution. Brussels airport sightings the same night were dropped after reporting cast doubt on them.

title: Explosives on a rail line serving Ukraine
summary: Explosives detonated under a freight train on the Warsaw–Lublin line; damage elsewhere halted a passenger train.
impact: Track and a freight train damaged; no injuries
note: Poland blamed Russian intelligence services; prosecutors charged two suspects who fled to Belarus.

title: Track and power lines damaged on the same line
summary: A metal brace was fixed across the tracks and power wires were brought down on the same line.
note: Same case as the Mika explosion.

target: Approach path of the Ukrainian president's plane
title: Drones near the Ukrainian president's flight path
summary: Several drones flew near the expected flight path of the Ukrainian president's plane; a navy ship observed them.
impact: None; the plane had already landed
note: The Irish prime minister linked the incident to tensions with Russia over frozen assets.

title: Two data cables damaged by a dragged anchor
summary: A cargo ship from St Petersburg was detained after its lowered anchor allegedly damaged two cables.
note: Finnish police suspect aggravated sabotage; Estonia said the ship did not appear to be part of the shadow fleet.

title: Explosives seized in a suspected bomb plot
summary: Two men were detained with explosives in their luggage, allegedly for an attack in Germany.
note: Investigators suspect a Russian-linked plot aimed at military supplies for Ukraine.

target: Airport, near a Ukrainian cargo plane
title: Explosive-laden drone found near a Ukrainian cargo plane
summary: A drone carrying explosives was found near a Ukrainian cargo aircraft and defused; a second object later hit a cargo plane near the airport.
impact: Airport closed for hours; minor damage to one aircraft
note: Germany's government concluded Russia was responsible and closed a Russian consulate. Russia rejected the accusation.

title: Fire and explosions at an ammunition store
summary: Fire and explosions destroyed an ammunition storage building belonging to the same arms company.
note: Fits the pattern of blasts at the same company that prosecutors linked to Russian military intelligence.

target: Construction site near a defence electronics company
title: Incendiary devices thrown at a defence company site
summary: Incendiary devices were thrown at a construction site near a defence company's headquarters; one started a fire.
note: Germany suspects Russian intelligence; two suspects were detained. Confirm with a German-language source.

title: Fire spreads across an ammunition store
summary: A fire and explosions spread from warehouse to warehouse at the same company's storage site.
note: Cause not yet determined; same pattern as the company's earlier blasts.
